_howto: One list per page. answer = the number of the right option, counting from 0. why = the explanation shown after any pick.

positions.why: Props are 1 (loosehead) and 3 (tighthead), on each side of the hooker.

positions.q: Who throws the ball in at every lineout?
positions.why: The hooker throws in at every lineout. It's their signature skill.

positions.q: In open play, where are the tight five?
positions.why: The tight five are in a center pod and carry the ball in a pod of 3.

positions.q: On the Phins, who lifts and jumps in the lineout?
options: Any forward, depending on the call
positions.why: Flexibility over labels! The only set job is the hooker's throw.

positions.q: Who is the only player who can pick the ball up from the base of the scrum?

vocab.q: At a ruck, can you use your hands on the ball?
vocab.why: A ruck means no hands allowed.

options: Joining a ruck or tackle from directly behind it
vocab.why: You must join through the gate, not from the side.

vocab.q: In a Phins pod, who is the "lead"?
options: The lead ball carrier, first to get the ball
The inside supporter near the ruck
vocab.why: Lead carries. Plus is the outside supporter. Lazy is the inside supporter near the ruck.

options: Diving or falling over the ball to protect it
vocab.why: Sealing off is illegal. Stay on your feet.

scrum.q: What are the ref's three scrum calls?
scrum.why: Crouch, Bind, Set. Engage only on Set.

scrum.q: What does 3-2-3 mean in a scrum?
scrum.why: Front row (props + hooker), second row (locks), back row (flankers + 8).

scrum.q: Where does the tighthead's (3) head go?
options: Between the opposing loosehead and hooker
scrum.why: That's why the tighthead takes pressure from both sides.
The 8 packs between the locks and controls the ball at the base.

scrum.q: What should locks NOT do on "Set"?
scrum.why: Hold on Set. Push once the ball is in.

options: When the ball goes out of bounds (into touch)
lineout.why: Lineouts restart play after the ball goes into touch.

lineout.q: Where does the throw have to go?
lineout.why: A not-straight throw gives the other team the choice of a lineout or scrum.
Lift on the thighs/shorts, hold, and bring the jumper down safely.

lineout.q: The forwards line up between which lines?
options: The try line and the 5m line
lineout.why: The lineout is between the 5m and 15m lines, two lines 1 meter apart.

options: Carry, tackle, ruck, ball out, next phase
openplay.why: Then it starts again for the next phase.

openplay.q: How big is a Phins pod?
Finish the Phins phrase: "Never go alone..."
openplay.why: Never go alone. Never let someone go alone.

options: The pass from the 9 to the 10
The space between the touch line and the 5m line
openplay.why: DO NOT BLOCK THE SACRED CHANNEL!

kickoffs.q: How far does a kickoff need to go?
kickoffs.why: It has to reach the 10m line.

kickoffs.q: Where is the kickoff taken from?
kickoffs.why: The center of halfway, at the start of each half and after scores.

kickoffs.q: Which restart happens when the ball is held up in your in-goal?
kickoffs.why: Held up in your in-goal means a goal line drop out.

pitch.q: Where do you ground the ball to score a try?
options: On or over the try line
pitch.why: On or over the try line, in the in-goal.

pitch.q: Kickoffs must go past which line?
pitch.why: If it doesn't reach the 10m line, the other team gets options.

pitch.q: What's the closest a scrum can be set to the try line?
pitch.why: Scrums and lineouts can't be set closer than the 5m line.

penalties.q: What can't you do with a free kick?
penalties.why: That's the big difference between a free kick and a penalty.

penalties.q: A knock-on gives the other team a...
penalties.why: Accidental mistakes like knock-ons and forward passes are scrums, not penalties.

penalties.q: Which one is a golden rule?
options: Join the ruck from the side
penalties.why: Stay on your feet. Come through the gate. Release. Roll away. Stay onside.

penalties.q: Pushing before the ref says "Set" at a scrum gives away a...
penalties.why: Early engagement is a free kick.

penalties.q: The ref's arm is bent at a right angle with the forearm straight up. What's that?
penalties.why: Bent arm is a free kick. A straight arm angled up is a penalty.

scoring.q: How many points is a try?
How many points is a conversion?
A penalty try (in Learn More) is worth...
scoring.why: Penalty tries are 7, no kick needed.

scoring.q: Why does scoring under the posts help?
scoring.why: Conversions are taken in line with where the try was scored.

tackling.q: Where does your head go in a tackle?
options: On the side of their butt/hip (cheek to cheek)
tackling.why: Never in front of their body.
Wrap with your arms. Drive with your legs.

first-match.q: Is it ok to be nervous before your first match?
first-match.why: Everyone gets nervous. Your team has your back.

first-match.q: Who is allowed to talk to the ref?
options: Anyone who disagrees with a call
first-match.why: NO ONE talks to the ref except the captains.

options: No, showing up is part of being a Phin
first-match.why: Both teams hang out after. It's a rugby tradition, and part of being a Phin.

first-match.q: You're subbed off. Can you go back on later?
options: No, unless it's a blood sub or all our props are injured
first-match.why: Once you're off, you're off, with those two exceptions.

safety.q: What's the number one way to prevent concussions?
options: Tackling and running with proper form

safety.q: You feel a little weird after a hit, but you're not sure. What do you do?
options: Come off and see the trainer
safety.why: You don't have to be sure. We want you safe and healthy.

safety.q: You have a headache after a hard hit. Who do you see?
safety.why: Dizzy, headache, or a hard hit: see the trainer.

calls.q: What does "Ball's out!" tell your team?
options: The ball has left the ruck
calls.why: The ruck is over and defenders can go.

calls.q: Why do we talk on the field?
options: So everyone knows where to be
calls.why: Talk! Communication keeps the chaos manageable.
